Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P2: The transaction commits all generated tasks before any audit is written. If `recordAudit` then fails, for example after membership is revoked, this action returns `{ ok: false, created: 0 }` while tasks remain persisted and un-audited; include audit writes in the transaction or handle audit failure without reporting task creation failure. P2: This retry bypasses the fake-mode no-provisioning invariant and can create an organization and membership from a fake session. Add `!fakeSessionActive()` to the condition before calling `provision`. P2: `current` is checked without a row lock, so `deleteTask` can remove it before the cross-column update; that branch then commits other position changes while updating zero task rows. Add `.for("update")` to this select. ```

**1 existing issue remains and 10 new issues found** across 46 files
Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P1: This predicate serializes concurrent closes but not `moveDeal`: a move that read an open deal can write afterward and reopen or retarget the deal after `closeDeal` returns and audits it. Add an optimistic expected-state guard or transaction/locking protocol to `moveDeal` so a close cannot be overwritten. P2: This test removes a shared production-schema index and does not restore it in a `finally` block. Run the setup in a disposable schema/database or use transactional isolation so a failed test cannot corrupt later tests or local development data. P2: This migration test validates duplicated SQL, not `drizzle/0014_daily-date-required.sql`; changing the migration will not affect the test. Execute the actual migration against a pre-0014 fixture in an isolated database/schema, or keep this as a clearly separate algorithm test. P2: This backfill can abort the entire seed when `ORG_WORKOS_ID` is already attached to a different organization. Look up the existing WorkOS-ID row and handle that collision explicitly before assigning the fixed ID. P3: These restores leave absent `WORKOS_*` variables as the literal `"undefined"`, contaminating subsequent tests and configuration checks in the same worker. Delete each key when its saved value is `undefined`, or use Vitest’s `vi.stubEnv`/`vi.unstubAllEnvs` for restoration. P1: `onConflictDoNothing()` also swallows conflicts on the unique `organizations.slug` constraint. If an existing unmapped organization already uses this WorkOS ID as its slug, provisioning commits an orphaned user with `needsOrg=false`, and subsequent logins permanently skip the retry path; restrict this clause to the `workosOrgId` conflict (or roll back when no mapped org is found). P1: This backfill can abort on the existing partial unique index before the dedupe executes: two manual rows with the same project, title, and due date become duplicate daily rows in one UPDATE. Reconcile those candidates first or temporarily drop and recreate the partial index around the backfill. P1: The dedupe leaves an earliest or lone `source='daily'` row with a NULL date, so `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT` still fails on valid pre-0014 database state. Demote or repair every dateless daily row before adding this CHECK. P2: `readColumn` snapshots task rows without locking them, so concurrent task deletion can invalidate the reorder snapshot and leave inconsistent positions. Lock the current task and both column snapshots with `FOR UPDATE`, or serialize task deletion on the project lock before calculating and persisting positions. P2: The reorder audit records a stale `from` status after the in-lock reread can observe an earlier queued move. Return the locked source status from the transaction and use it in the audit metadata. ```
